brief: With ~40 days to the US midterms, a Democratic House flip is viewed as near-certain (90% odds among conference speakers, forecasts point to a 220-230 seat majority), while the Senate remains a toss-up: the GOP holds 53-47 and needs Democrats to flip 4 seats, with betting markets giving the GOP only a 36% chance of holding it. Affordability dominates voter sentiment (25% satisfied vs a 33% historical average), and the Iran conflict has pushed Brent to $100-110/bbl from a $75-100 band seen since May, shifting momentum toward Democrats since elevated gas prices historically add about 5 House seats to the incumbent party's losses. Populist backlash to 'AI winners' is rising regardless of outcome, even as comprehensive AI regulation stays unlikely near-term due to state-level fragmentation, a constraint expected to lift after Nov 3. Post-midterm, policy volatility is expected to skew higher: a lame-duck Trump is expected to keep governing via executive action (285 EOs already, more than his full first term), with risk from a possible $300-500bn reconciliation package, Section 301 tariffs lifting the effective tariff rate toward 17-18%, debt-ceiling brinksmanship pressuring Treasuries, and an intensifying US-Canada trade war.
